recipes.name: Lemon Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant lemon pudding mix
1 (1 ounce) package instant sugar-free vanilla pudding mix
1 (8 ounce) container frozen light whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray a 10x15-inch baking pan with nonstick spray.

Make the cake: In a large bowl, mix together cake mix and lemon pudding mix. Pour in water and egg whites. Beat with an electric mixer on low speed for 1 minute. Increase the speed to high and beat for 4 minutes. Pour batter into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes. Remove from the oven and allow to cool completely, 20 to 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the topping: In a large bowl, beat milk, vanilla pudding mix, and lemon extract on low speed for 2 minutes. Fold in whipped topping. Spread over the cooled cake. Store cake in the refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Cake
raw_recipe.description: This lemon cake recipe features a lemon sheet cake topped with a lemony whipped topping. Cake mix and two kinds of pudding mix make this so simple!

review.reviewBody: Great cake!! I used a lemon cake and added a few tablespoons of fresh lemon juice in place of some of the water in the cake. My coworkers gobbled this up and my boss wanted the recipe after I took this to a work luncheon. Will definitely make again, very refreshing and light tasting!

I made this for my daughter's birthday and everyone loved it! Used 9 x 13 pan, lemon cake mix, and lemon pudding. As someone else said, be sure to beat batter for the full time and cake will rise nicely.

Delicious lower calorie cake! I used a package of sugar free instant lemon pudding mix in both the cake and the topping. I did not add the lemon extract to the topping. I used 4 egg whites instead of 3 and used 1 1/3 c water (wanted to compensate for cake mixes now being 3 oz smaller than most recipes list). I loved that the cake had a light texture and a very fine, almost smooth crumb, but was not at all gummy or rubbery. A delightful dessert.

I am the first to admit, I am NOT a baker. Cakes have always intimidated me (not sure why really). My husband has been begging me to make him a cake, more specifically a Lemon cake, so after scouring the internet for over an hr I settled on this recipe. I read most of the reviews prior to starting this endeavor and so glad I did. Here are the tweaks I made...I, too, used lemon cake mix (instead of vanilla). My husband was very specific on "wanting it lemony" so I used 1 cup water and 3/4 fresh lemon juice (about 5 lemons). I also made this in 2-9in cake pans, cooking about 25 min. I used 1 egg and 2 egg whites (the cake did turn out pretty dense like a pound cake). I didn't have lemon extract, so used 1/2 tsp lemon zest (thank GOD for google). Best part of all, I used real heavy whipping cream (1 pint) instead of cool whip. As an experiment (yeah i live on the edge as a rookie) I took 1/4 or so of the whipped topping and mixed with about 2 tbsp of red raspberry preserves and put in the middle layer (of the 2-9in cakes) SO GOOD! Even my picky picky husband was impressed. Kudos to me!

Delicious!

Caution: Check the size of your cake mix before you start. A lot of the big brands no longer sell 18.25 oz cake mixes. They're almost all 15.25 oz. Your cake will be heavy and wet if you don't adjust your recipe. I added 6 tbsp of all-purpose flour which worked well for me.

I'm guessing that's why most of the bad reviews are newer and the best reviews are 2012 or earlier.

I also made my own lemon pudding (because I suddenly had three spare egg yolks) which I then mixed with the 'whipped topping'. 

It was fantastic! I like the topping for this rather than standard buttercream icing and might adjust it for use with other cakes.

I have made this recipe twice and both times everyone loved it. The first time I made it I used white cake mix and lemon pudding mix. I had lemon frosting on hand and used that. I followed the other reviewers' advice to make sure the cake was mixed for the right amount of time and used a 9 x 13 pan. The cake was super moist. The lemon frosting give it an extra lemon flavor. The second time I made the cake I used lemon cake mix and lemon pudding mix. I made the frosting with whipped topping and lemon pudding mix. It also came out moist and with a great lemon flavor that is not overpowering. Thank you LaDonna for this wonderful recipe. It will be my go to recipe when I want to make a lemon cake.

This cake is seriously awesome if you pay attention to a few details . The most helpful review was the one that mentions making sure the cake mix you buy and the instant pudding you buy match the measurements the recipe calls for. My lemon cake mix was not the proper weight so I added some flour to make up the difference. And my pudding mix was too large so I only used a partial pack. Also, using fresh lemon juice for half of the water the recipe calls for makes an amazing difference! I also added lemon zest of two lemons into the mix. Seriously incredible tasting cake. Use a lemon flavoured cake mix for sure.

I made this for my mom for her birthday and she loved it!! I did make some adjustments though. I used a lemon cake mix and I used 1/2 cup of fresh lemon juice in place of some of the water. I made my own frosting. One 8oz package of cream cheese, 1 cup powdered sugar, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice and 16oz cool whip. Blend the ingredients together and spread on cake. Refrigerate and serve.

Made this for Easter dessert, was delicious! Had a great lemon flavor. Folks even went back for 2nds. As others have recommended I used a lemon cake mix and followed directions on box but cut water down by 2 tablespoons and added 2 tablespoons of fresh lemon juice. Made in 13X9 pan. 
For the icing substituted lemon pudding for the vanilla and was very tasty. This is a keeper and will make again.

This cake was delicious. I made it for a dinner with friends and everyone loved it. I did end up using a lemon cake and used a few tablespoons of lemon juice mixed in with the water. Also for those that said it was runny, be very careful about looking at the sizes of your pudding, as some sizes are larger than others. I used to whole eggs and one egg white and it was just right. My cake raised just fine in the oven. for the frosting I added an 8 oz package of cream cheese and some powdered sugar just because I like more of the rich texture for the frosting. Will definitely make again!

Made it today for family gathering and was asked to make it for a birthday party in a few weeks.
Changes I made: I added a thin layer of strawberry jam between layers and secured with toothpicks until I was ready to add topping. Removed toothpicks before topping and served with assorted berries on the top and sides of serving plate for a more festive presentation. 
Notes: very dense cake, more like pound cake than box cake mix is typically. Does not rise very much. Kept refrigerated before and after adding topping and berries, chilling enhances refreshing aspect of this dessert.

This recipe has so many problems. First, the pan size. The batter doesn't even coat a 10x15 pan. Why has no one mentioned this? So I used a standard 9x13 instead. It resulted in a 1" thick, bizarre, rubbery, spongey semblance of a "cake." When it cooled, it shrunk and left a 1" gap from the pan edges. So weird. Then, using a sugar-free pudding mix in the topping gave it that unpleasant chemical flavor. I added fresh lemon juice in the batter, and lemon zest in the topping, and the thing barely tastes lemony (though I have no plans to actually ingest this disaster). I cannot understand how this recipe has any stars at all. Zero stars for me.

This cake was lemony delicious. I left out the egg whites....accidentally. it made the cake a little denser, but it was still awesome. Can't wait to make it again. Next time I'll remember to add the egg whites.

I listened to all the reviews and used lemon cake mix and lemon pudding in the frosting. The flavor was really good but I did notice a funny aftertaste that another reviewer also mentioned. Also, this cake was dense and thick, not an airy or light cake, which is fine just different. Overall it was tasty but I’d probably try a different recipe next time.

I am en experienced baker who usually bakes from scratch. But I needed something fast and tasty, so after reading the glowing reviews I decided to try this recipe.

I am extremely disappointed in it. Followed the directions EXACTLY, yet this cake did not rise. It was very moist -- but very flat. What a shamw because it was meant for my best friend's birthday. Will not make this again. It's a shame I must give it a one star review.

Very moist and excellent lemon taste. Followed recipe since my store didn’t carry lemon cake mix. Added lemon zest to cake mix and to topping to ensure it would taste lemony, Turned out great, and we all loved it!

I used this recipe only for the cake part, and while it is a perfectly edible cake, I kept asking myself “what is the point of this cake?“ It uses a cake mix, but deviates from the directions on the box, and produces a cake that has a strange texture – kind of like a cross between a poundcake and an angel food cake, if you can imagine that. Honestly, I would have enjoyed a cake made from a cake mix, according to the directions on the box, more than this.

I’ve been making a version of this cake for years. This recipe will produce a delicately flavored lemon cake, however it was written years ago before the sly cake mix people made the mixes smaller. Prior to 2011 cake mixes were 18.25 oz. Now they’re 15.25 oz. I know, I also feel betrayed.

I made this recipe two weeks in a row for my 9-year old lemon-loving son who requested lemon cake as his birthday cake (made cupcakes). After reading many of the reviews along with trial and error, I can say without hesitation that whipping the egg whites first and then folding them in is essential to the consistency of the cake. Additionally, per many recommendations, I used lemon cake mix & part real lemon juice in lieu of water (I juiced three lemons, then added water to equate to 1 3/4 cup). To save time, I used store-bought lemon frosting so I can't comment on the topping.
Tastes so gooooood!
